source: ESPN NBA league injury designations plus NBA game lineup state

freshnessPolicy.missingReportMeaning: No injury report was matched; this is not a confirmed healthy designation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Flemings (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Flemings left Friday's 125-117 loss to Chicago with back tightness after playing 17 minutes. The ailment will keep the rookie first-rounder on the sidelines Sunday, with veteran CJ McCollum the likely candidate to join the starting lineup. Flemings' next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus Oklahoma City.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Gilbert (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Bulls.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Gilbert continues to deal with lingering knee inflammation and is without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Hawks offer an update on his progress.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Newell (toe) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Chicago.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Newell will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left great toe hyperextension. He can be considered week-to-week until the Hawks provide an update on his progress.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Miller (groin) is listed as out for Thursday's game against Phoenix.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Miller injured his groin during the 119-80 loss to Boston on Friday and subsequently missed Monday's meeting with Cleveland. Now that Miller is confirmed to be sidelined for a second consecutive contest, Sion James is the favorite to remain in the starting lineup.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Watson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Watson will join the rest of Cleveland's regular starters on the inactive list. The 24-year-old's next chance to play will come Monday against Chicago. With Watson sidelined, Jaylon Tyson and Mario Hezonja will likely see increased playing time.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Mobley (toe) has been ruled out for Saturday's meeting with Dallas.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Mobley will miss a second consecutive contest due to a left great toe sprain, and his next chance to play will come Monday against the Bulls. Jarrett Allen (knee) is questionable for Saturday's contest, so Thomas Bryant could be asked to step into an expanded role.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Tomlin is set to miss several weeks with a lower back stress reaction, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: This is a tough blow for the forward and there's no guarantee he's cleared right away when he's re-evaluated in three-to-four weeks. Tomlin wasn't projected to crack the rotation ahead of Opening Night and was penciled in to be an emergency depth option.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Thursday's game in Minnesota.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Lively is still working his way back from foot surgery. He's reportedly trending favorably, though he should continue to be classified as week-to-week, at least until the team provides an update. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford is expected to stay in the starting lineup, with Morez Johnson (shin), Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse all in line to spend time at the five when needed.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: De Larrea (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game at Minnesota.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: De Larrea hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a right knee sprain, but he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Still, he can be considered week-to-week until Dallas provides an update on his progress.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Williams (hamstring) will miss at least one week, per Anthony Slater of ESPN.com.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Williams has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain in the aftermath of Monday's game against the Pelicans, and his status for Golden State's upcoming five-game road trip is in serious doubt. With Williams facing an extended absence, the Warriors are likely to lean more on De'Anthony Melton in the backourt.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Capela (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Washington.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Capela is trending toward a return to action, though he'll remain sidelined Sunday due to a right ankle sprain. His next chance to suit up will come Monday at Miami.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Adams (calf) has been upgraded to probable for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Head coach Ime Udoka said Monday that Adams could be ready to play by Sunday, and that seems even more likely now that the veteran center carries a probable tag. Adams hasn't played since Oct. 23, so the Rockets may look to ease him back into things.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: VanVleet (right knee injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: VanVleet will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday at Miami. With the veteran floor general sidelined, Reed Sheppard, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Bruce Thornton are candidates for increased playing time, while Amen Thompson figures to see increased on-ball duties.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Smart has been suspended three games for throwing a punch during Wednesday's matchup against Golden State, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Smart, who was ejected from Wednesday's game for punching Charles Bassey, will begin serving his suspension Friday night against the Jazz, meaning he'll be eligible to return Wednesday versus Indiana. Bruce Thornton and Reed Sheppard should be in line for more minutes while Smart serves his three-game ban.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: McConnell (hamstring) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against the 76ers.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: McConnell missed the Pacers' first nine games of the season due to hamstring problems, and although he still seems to be working through the injury, he's been able to play in each of Indiana's last four contests. The fact that he's been listed as probable is a positive sign that he'll suit up for a fifth straight game Sunday.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Nesmith (hand) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Philadelphia.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Nesmith suffered a left hand sprain in the final seconds of Friday's win over the Knicks and could be held out of Sunday's road game. If the veteran swingman is unable to suit up, Jarace Walker, Quenton Jackson and Jalen Slawson would be candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Rick Carlisle said Wednesday that Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least 10 more days, Alex Golden of SI.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Haliburton is still recovering from a left hamstring strain and will need more time to ramp up. Andrew Nembhard should continue seeing increased on-ball duties in Haliburton's stead, while Quenton Jackson and Braden Smith are also candidates for increased burn.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Ingram (Achilles) won't play in Friday's game against the Thunder, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Ingram is ramping up his activity as he nears his season debut for the Clippers, but he's not yet cleared for game action amid his Achilles rehab. Until the star forward is ready to suit up, Kris Dunn, Rui Hachimura and Derrick Jones should all hang onto starting roles.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Niederhauser (foot) is out for Tuesday's game against Phoenix, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Niederhauser has yet to make an appearance this season for the Clippers while rehabbing from foot surgery. It's unclear at this time when he'll be available to take the court, and he can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Sexton (head) was a full participant in Saturday's practice, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Sexton left Wednesday's game against Milwaukee early after bumping heads with Ryan Rollins and required stitches to close a cut on his forehead. However, Sexton escaped the incident without a concussion, and his ability to practice without restraint is a positive sign for his availability Sunday against the Suns.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Reaves (heel) didn't participate in Saturday's practice, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Reaves sustained a bruised left heel in Wednesday's win over Milwaukee and is considered day-to-day, though this update is not encouraging ahead of Sunday's game against Phoenix. If the 28-year-old guard is unable to suit up, Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes (finger) and Collin Sexton (head) would be candidates for increased playing time.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Grimes (finger) said he expects to return to action Sunday against the Suns, according to Ricardo Sandoval of Lakers on SI.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games, but it sounds as if he could return to the rotation Sunday. It's unclear whether he'd be a starter, but he'd have a chance if Austin Reaves (heel) isn't cleared. Grimes is averaging 8.0 points per game this season, but that number rises to 17.5 points per game in his two starts.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Dieng (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Dieng is dealing with a left finger sprain and will miss Sunday's contest after logging just five minutes while starting Friday's loss to the Magic. Nate Ament could see a slight bump in minutes in Dieng's stead.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Mitchell (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Mitchell will miss a second consecutive contest due to a let ankle sprain, and his next chance to play will come Sunday at Sacramento. With the 24-year-old guard out, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford are candidates for increased playing time.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Sorber (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Sorber is still recovering from knee surgery and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Thunder offer an update on his status.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Williams (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Portland and remains out indefinitely.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Williams is slated to miss a fifth straight game and doesn't have a return timetable, so it's fair to consider him week-to-week. With Chet Holmgren (knee) also sidelined, the Thunder will rely on Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Isaac (knee) is out for Tuesday's game against Sacramento.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Isaac has yet to make his 2026-27 debut while continuing his rehab from a left knee injury. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Wednesday in Utah.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Embiid (right foot injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pacers.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Embiid will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set. With Adem Bona (back) and Dominick Barlow (back) sidelined, Dean Wade, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall could all see increased playing time, while LeBron James could also see more time at the five as well.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Barlow (back) participated in Thursday's shootaround but doesn't have a timeline to return to game action, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Barlow has been dealing with back soreness dating back to the preseason, so his participation in shootaround is an encouraging step. However, the 76ers have yet to provide a firm return date, and he'll likely need to ramp up further before he's cleared to play. Barlow should be monitored in deeper formats, but he isn't someone who needs to be rostered while he remains sidelined.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: The Suns claimed Timme off waivers Monday, per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: After being let go by Minnesota on Saturday, Timme wasn't allowed to go through waivers unclaimed without Phoenix snatching him up. With Mark Williams (shoulder) likely out through the All-Star break, Timme helps reinforce Phoenix's depth at center.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Youngblood (foot) is out for Friday's game against Sacramento.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Youngblood is in line for a second straight absence due to a bone bruise in his right foot. His next opportunity to run the floor will arrive Monday in Minnesota.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Murray (illness) didn't participate in Saturday's practice, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Murray is dealing with an illness ahead of Sunday's home game against the Thunder. If he's unable to play, De'Andre Hunter and Dylan Cardwell would likely see increased burn, especially if Precious Achiuwa (ankle) remains out.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Achiuwa (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Trail Blazers.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Achiuwa is sitting out Friday for the first time this season due to left ankle soreness, and he can be deemed day-to-day going forward. His absence likely paves the way for Keegan Murray to re-enter the starting lineup after opening 2026-27 as the Kings' starting power forward.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Raynaud (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Orlando.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Raynaud is expected to be re-evaluated soon, though he can be considered week-to-week until the Kings offer an update on his status. Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa will likely continue seeing increased burn in Raynaud's absence.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Harris (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Chicago, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: With Harris still sidelined, San Antonio will rely more on Julian Champagnie. Harris has yet to make his Spurs debut this season, so his absence continues to leave minutes available on the wing until he is cleared to return.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.ca reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Bittle is still working his way back from a foot fracture that has plagued him for multiple months, and he remains without a clear return timeline. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Barnes (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Barnes has missed four straight games with a groin strain, but he was able to participate partially in practice Saturday. Collin Murray-Boyles would presumably pick up another start at power forward if Barnes' absence continues.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: McCullar signed a two-way contract with the Raptors on Thursday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: McCullar quickly finds a new home after being waived by the Knicks in late October. The forward is expected to play a prominent role for Toronto's G League affiliate.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Darko Rajakovic said Wednesday that Leonard (knee) is doing individual on-court work and is progressing well, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The Raptors are expected to provide another update on Leonard's status in about one week, though it's encouraging to see how he's progressed thus far. Collin Murray-Boyles and Ja'Kobe Walter are candidates for increased playing time for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Hayes won't return to Friday's game against the Rockets due to a left knee issue.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Hayes will end up missing the entire second half. He was playing well prior to the injury, finishing with 12 points on 5-of-6 shooting with five rebounds and one assist in 13 minutes. Mo Bamba could be in line for more run with this news.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Sarr (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Houston.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Sarr is under the weather and could miss the front end of this back-to-back set. The big man's absence would open up additional minutes for guys like Deandre Ayton, Anthony Gill and Will Riley.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Johnson is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Rockets due to lower-back soreness.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Johnson has logged at least 27 minutes in each of Washington's last five games, but a back injury could prevent him from facing Houston on Sunday. If he and Bub Carrington (chest) are both ruled out, Will Riley could play meaningful minutes against the Rockets.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Carrington (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Houston.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Carrington exited Thursday's loss to Detroit with a chest contusion and is now in jeopardy of missing his first game of the season. If the third-year guard is ruled out, Tre Mann and Will Riley could see increased burn, especially if Tre Johnson (back) is also downgraded from questionable to out.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Detroit.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip impingement. The big man can be viewed as week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

injury.shortComment: Mathurin is out for Saturday's game against the Nuggets due to left plantar fasciitis.
injury.detail: Mathurin will miss a second game of the Pelicans' last three, leaving New Orleans without a key second-unit scorer. Mathurin is averaging 5.5 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists across 15.3 minutes per game so far. His next chance to suit up will come Monday at home against the Warriors.

injury.shortComment: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nuggets.
injury.detail: McGowens will miss his second game in as many days while continuing to deal with a left elbow infection. He'll have another chance to return to action Monday against the Warriors.

injury.shortComment: Murphy (knees) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nuggets.
injury.detail: Murphy will miss a fourth straight game as he continues to battle bilateral patellar tendinopathy. His next opportunity to return to the court will come Monday against the Warriors. Saddiq Bey should continue to work in an elevated role in the meantime.

injury.shortComment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
injury.detail: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

injury.shortComment: Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Denver.
injury.detail: Watford will miss a fourth consecutive game Saturday due to a right ankle sprain, and it remains unknown how far away he is from returning.

injury.shortComment: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
injury.detail: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

injury.shortComment: Allen (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
injury.detail: Allen will get a break to rest his injured right knee after playing in each of Cleveland's last three games. With Evan Mobley (toe) also out, Thomas Bryant can be expected to take on a larger role Saturday.

injury.shortComment: Harden (calf) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Dallas.
injury.detail: Harden will miss his first game of the season due to a calf issue he picked up sometime after Friday's loss to Miami. Fellow guard Donovan Mitchell (knee) will also be inactive Saturday, leaving Tyrese Proctor, Craig Porter and Meleek Thomas as Cleveland's top backcourt options.

injury.shortComment: Merrill (elbow) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
injury.detail: Merrill has battled a lingering elbow issue since the preseason. He will now miss a third consecutive contest, with his next opportunity to suit up coming Friday in Miami. While Merrill is sidelined, Craig Porter, Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor should see more minutes.

injury.shortComment: Mitchell (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
injury.detail: Mitchell will miss his first game of the season due to a left knee contusion. The Cavaliers will be without all of their usual starters, meaning Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas and Craig Porter should all see significant minutes in the backcourt.

injury.shortComment: Christie (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Cleveland.
injury.detail: Christie was doubtful to play due to a left ankle sprain, and he will indeed be forced to sit out his second contest of the 2026-27 campaign. Expect Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher to see a boost in minutes.

injury.shortComment: Biberovic (heel) is out for Thursday's game against Minnesota.
injury.detail: Biberovic remains plagued by right heel bursitis. The rookie forward carries no timetable for his season debut.

injury.shortComment: Larsson (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Pistons.
injury.detail: Larsson was listed as doubtful to play earlier in the day, and he's now officially been ruled out due to an illness. He'll miss a second consecutive game after sitting out Friday's 133-121 win over Cleveland. Myron Gardner earned the start in Larsson's absence, while Andrew Wiggins and rookie Ryan Conwell each played 30-plus minutes off Miami's bench. Fantasy managers can expect a similar trend versus Detroit.

injury.shortComment: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

injury.shortComment: Joe (hip) is out for Monday against the Wizards.
injury.detail: Joe is missing a seventh consecutive contest with a bruised hip. His next chance to play comes Thursday in a road rematch with Washington.

injury.shortComment: Onyenso agreed to a two-way contract with the Pistons on Thursday.
injury.detail: The No. 53 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Onyenso appears poised to see run in the G League after putting pen to paper on a two-way deal. He'll likely face an uphill battle to carve out a role in the rotation, so Detroit will presumably allow him to continue his development with Motor City.

injury.shortComment: Edey (ankle) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Brooklyn.
injury.detail: Edey sat out Memphis' game Friday due to an ankle injury, and he is now at risk of missing both legs of this back-to-back set. With Quinten Post (concussion) already having been ruled out, Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks remain the likely candidates to pick up extra minutes if Edey doesn't play.

injury.shortComment: Grant (head) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Nets.
injury.detail: Grant could be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a head injury. If the veteran forward is unable to suit up, Kris Murray and GG Jackson would likely see increased burn.

injury.shortComment: Jerome (hip) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
injury.detail: Jerome is dealing with right hip soreness and will miss his second game of the season. With the veteran guard joining Scotty Pippen (back) on the inactive list, Cam Spencer figures to see an expanded role. Jerome's next opportunity to play will come Monday at Washington.

injury.shortComment: Pippen (back) remains out for Wednesday's game against Denver, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
injury.detail: With Pippen set to miss another game, Memphis will continue to operate without one of its backcourt reserves. He has now been sidelined for six straight contests due to the back issue and can be considered week-to-week until Memphis offers an update on his recovery. Cam Spencer remains worth streaming in most fantasy leagues.

injury.shortComment: Post (concussion) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
injury.detail: Saturday will mark Post's third straight missed game as he remains in the league's concussion protocol. His next chance to play will come Monday at Washington.

injury.shortComment: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

injury.shortComment: Porter (personal) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Memphis, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injury.detail: Porter was a late addition to the injury report due to a personal issue. If the veteran misses his first game of the 2026-27 campaign Saturday, Keon Ellis, Terance Mann and Danny Wolf could all see more minutes.

injury.shortComment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
injury.detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

injury.shortComment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injury.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

injury.shortComment: Awaka has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
injury.detail: Now set to miss a third straight game due to a back injury, Awaka will aim to return during Chicago's next game against Cleveland on Monday.

injury.shortComment: Claxton (hamstring) is out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
injury.detail: Claxton was carrying a questionable tag ahead of Saturday's contest, and the big man will miss the game -- his first absence since his season debut Nov. 8 against the 76ers. Claxton will aim to return to action against the Cavaliers on Monday. With Claxton and Jalen Smith (finger) out, Zach Collins and Orlando Robinson are expected to see most of the minutes at center.

injury.shortComment: Smith (finger) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Minnesota, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
injury.detail: Smith will miss his first game of the season after being listed questionable earlier Saturday due to a sprained left finger. Nix Claxton (hamstring) has also been ruled out, leaving Zach Collins and Orlando Robinson as the two healthy bigs remaining for Chicago.

injury.shortComment: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.
